title: Compactification coherence
statement:
Let $K_0$ be a field, let $X,Y$ be
finite-type $K_0$-schemes, and let
$f:X\to Y$ be a
separated finite-type
$K_0$-morphism. Fix a prime $\ell$, write $\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, and
require that its image in $K_0$ is invertible. Choose a finite extension
$E/\Ql$, an integer $n\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$,
and put $A=A_{E,n}$. The coefficient $A$ is used with the
finite-torsion
constructibility condition. For objects
$c_i=(j_i,\bar f_i)\in\operatorname{Comp}(f)$ in the
compactification category
and a refinement
$u:c_1\to c_2$, the canonical transformation between the
compact-support candidates

$$
R\bar f_{1*,n}j_{1!}
\xrightarrow{\sim}
R\bar f_{2*,n}j_{2!}
$$

is the composite of the proper-composition isomorphism with the isomorphism

$$
Ru_*j_{1!}\xrightarrow{\sim}j_{2!}
$$

on the ambient derived category. These transformations are identities for
identity refinements and are transitive under composition. For any two
compactifications $c_1,c_2$, comparison through a common refinement gives
a natural isomorphism

$$
Rf_{!,n}^{c_1}\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_{!,n}^{c_2}.
$$

Here $R\bar f_{i*,n}$ and $j_{i!}$ are respectively the
derived direct image and
extension-by-zero functors. A common
refinement may be chosen for any finite collection of
compactifications; the resulting comparison is independent of that choice
and satisfies the cocycle condition for triples of compactifications.
The comparison is asserted on the domain declared in
[def-weil-compact-support-candidate]: the complexes of the pro-etale
site that come from the etale site with an
etale-origin witness. It is
not asserted, and not claimed anywhere in the blueprint, on the whole of
$D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$.

proof.text: Write $T_i=\overline X_i$, $p_i=\bar f_i$, and $J_i=j_{i!}$. A refinement is proper and satisfies $u j_1=j_2$ and $p_2u=p_1$ by [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. The scheme $\operatorname{Spec}K_0$ is Noetherian: its only ideals are $(0),(1)$, and its one-point space is quasi-compact. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] first to $X,Y$ over this spectrum and then to $T_i\to Y$. The latter maps are of finite type because they are proper [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Thus all schemes to which the proper-open lemma will be applied are Noetherian. We will also use comparison of direct images for $u$: it is quasi-compact because it is of finite type; its diagonal is a closed immersion, hence proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] (c), hence of finite type and quasi-compact by the same two definitions. Thus $u$ is quasi-separated as well. These arguments apply to every refinement used below; no assumption that its square over $X$ is cartesian is made. All these schemes are $K_0$-schemes through their structure maps to $Y$, so the image of $\ell$ remains invertible on them, as required for finite-level derived composition.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 1: hypotheses for the proper-open comparison; Stacks Tags 01T6 (lemma-finite-type-noetherian), 01W1 (definition-proper), 01W5 (lemma-closed-immersion-proper)

proof.text:
First check naturality of the ordinary etale proper-open map, instead of inferring naturality from its being an objectwise isomorphism. Use the notation of [def-weil-pbc-proper-open-comparison]: $V=T_1\times_{T_2}X$, with $b,p,s$, and $\vartheta_L=c_L\,Rp_*(e_L)\,r_L:j_2^{-1}Ru_*j_{1!}L\to L$. The definition supplies the clopen section and the open-immersion square, so the hypotheses of the following three cited statements hold. The map $r$ is natural by [lem-weil-pbc-derived-open-restriction], and $e$ is natural by [cor-cbc-derived-extension-zero-base-change]. The map $c_L:Rp_*s_!L\to L$ of [lem-weil-pbc-clopen-section-direct-image] is restriction to the section component: restriction before or after a morphism $h:L\to L'$ gives the same map on that component, so $c_{L'}Rp_*s_!(h)=h c_L$. (On complexes the equation is degreewise; it is preserved under passage to the derived category.) Substituting these three equations in the composite gives $\vartheta_{L'}j_2^{-1}Ru_*j_{1!}(h)=h\vartheta_L$. The specified comparison is $a^{\mathrm{et}}_u(L)=\varepsilon\,j_{2!}(\vartheta_L^{-1})$. Inverting the preceding equation and using naturality of the adjunction counit $\varepsilon$ therefore gives
$$Ru_*j_{1!}(h)\,a^{\mathrm{et}}_u(L)=a^{\mathrm{et}}_u(L')\,j_{2!}(h).$$
This proves the needed naturality directly from the defining map, including when $u^{-1}(X)$ has an extra clopen component.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 1: naturality of the comparison used there, expanded using the specified adjoint construction; Stacks Tags 03DI (lemma-extension-by-zero) and 03DJ (lemma-extension-by-zero-exact) for extension by zero and its counit

proof.text: Construct the natural isomorphism on bounded-below etale objects directly from the four factors defining properOpenProEtaleIsoPlus in [lem-weil-pbc-proper-open-comparison-proetale]: inverse extension comparison, the etale proper/open natural isomorphism of step 2, the direct-image comparison of [prop-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image], and extension comparison under proper direct image. All factors are natural. The exact extension comparisons are the termwise derived maps of [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison], using [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact] and [def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback]. Its component is the specified properOpenProEtaleIsoPlus by definition. Whisker with the canonical bounded-below inclusions and the exact-functor and right-derived compatibility isomorphisms. The resulting natural isomorphism has exactly the component properOpenProEtaleIso of [lem-weil-pbc-proper-open-comparison-proetale], again by its definition. Thus its naturality gives the required square in the ambient derived category. No separate site-normalization theorem is needed.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 1: etale/pro-etale transport; source of the proper-open lemma, Proof paragraphs 1-3; Stacks Tags 09AF (lemma-jshriek-comparison), 09A6 (lemma-morphism-comparison), 03DJ (lemma-extension-by-zero-exact)

proof.text:
An object of the actual domain is a triple $(K,L,\eta)$ with $\eta:\nu_X^*L\xrightarrow{\sim}K$, and its morphisms are all ambient morphisms of $K$, by [def-sf-etale-origin-subcategory]. Transport the preceding map by the formula in [def-sf-refinement-comparison-isomorphism] (a):
$$A_u(K,L,\eta)=Ru_*J_1(\eta)\,a_u(L)\,J_2(\eta)^{-1}:J_2K\xrightarrow{\sim}Ru_*J_1K.$$
For any $k:K\to K'$ between witnessed objects, full faithfulness in [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] supplies a unique $h:L\to L'$ with $\nu_X^*h=\eta'^{-1}k\eta$. Substitute this equality in step 3 and multiply by the displayed witness maps. The result is
$$Ru_*J_1(k)\,A_u(K,L,\eta)=A_u(K',L',\eta')\,J_2(k).$$
This proves naturality for every morphism of the full domain, not only for maps presented in advance as pullbacks. If two witnesses are attached to the same $K$, apply this equation with $k=\operatorname{id}_K$; the two maps $A_u$ agree. In particular the comparison is independent of the witness after forgetting it.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 1 and last paragraph: extend from literal pullbacks to the declared full category with witnesses; Stacks Tag 099V (lemma-relative-comparison)

proof.text:
Put $\beta_u=A_u^{-1}:Ru_*J_1\xrightarrow{\sim}J_2$ on the domain of step 4. By [lem-weil-derived-direct-image-composition] (1), $C_{p_2,u}:Rp_{1*}\xrightarrow{\sim}Rp_{2*}Ru_*$ is defined on all finite-coefficient pro-etale complexes. The candidates are $F_i=Rf_{!,n}^{c_i}=Rp_{i*}J_i$ by [def-weil-compact-support-candidate]. Their comparison is exactly the composite specified in [def-sf-refinement-comparison-isomorphism] (b):
$$t_u=Rp_{2*}(\beta_u)\,C_{p_2,u}(J_1):F_1\xrightarrow{\sim}F_2.$$
Every component is invertible. For $k:K\to K'$, the equation of step 4 inverted gives naturality of $\beta_u$, and the stated naturality of $C_{p_2,u}$ gives $F_2(k)t_u(K)=t_u(K')F_1(k)$ after composition of the two squares. Hence $t_u$ is a natural isomorphism of the restricted candidate functors, with exactly the formula asserted in the statement.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 2, first two sentences: composition isomorphism followed by the inverse proper-open comparison

proof.text: Apply lem-sf-refinement-comparison-witness-comp after deriving Noetherianity of each compactification ambient from its proper map to Y and finite type of Y over the field. This proves the pointwise composition law. Extensionality assembles it to the composition law of the natural isomorphisms. For an identity refinement, composition of that refinement with itself gives theta = theta followed by theta; cancel the invertible theta to obtain theta = identity.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, last sentence; detailed proof step 6

proof.text:
For compactifications $c_1,c_2$, [prop-compactification-refinement] gives $d$ and arrows $a_i:d\to c_i$. Define $T_{12}^{d}=t_{a_2}t_{a_1}^{-1}:F_1\xrightarrow{\sim}F_2$. It is natural, since both factors are natural by step 5: for $k$, substitute the naturality equation for $t_{a_1}^{-1}$ and then the equation for $t_{a_2}$. If $q:e\to d$ is a further refinement, step 6 gives
$$t_{a_2q}t_{a_1q}^{-1}=(t_{a_2}t_q)(t_{a_1}t_q)^{-1}=t_{a_2}t_{a_1}^{-1}.$$
Thus passage to a further refinement leaves the comparison unchanged. This uses actual invertibility of $t_q$, already established, not a faithfulness assertion about pushforward.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 3: define comparison through a common refinement and check invariance under a further refinement

proof.text:
To prove independence of arbitrary choices of both the common refinement and its arrows, let $a_i:d\to c_i$ and $a_i':d'\to c_i$ be two choices. By [prop-compactification-refinement], choose $r:e\to d$ and $r':e\to d'$. Equalize the parallel arrows $a_1r,a_1'r'$ by a further $q_1:e_1\to e$. Then equalize $a_2rq_1,a_2'r'q_1$ by $q_2:e_2\to e_1$. Both equalities now hold on $e_2$, since precomposition preserves the first equality. Put $s=rq_1q_2$, $s'=r'q_1q_2$. Step 6 gives $t_{a_i}t_s=t_{a_i'}t_{s'}$ for $i=1,2$, and cancellation gives
$$t_{a_2}t_{a_1}^{-1}=(t_{a_2}t_s)(t_{a_1}t_s)^{-1}=(t_{a_2'}t_{s'})(t_{a_1'}t_{s'})^{-1}=t_{a_2'}t_{a_1'}^{-1}.$$
In particular a choice of different arrows from the same common refinement also gives the same transformation. No uniqueness of a refinement arrow is assumed.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 3: the two successive parallel-refinement equalizations and independence of choices

proof.text:
For any finite family of compactifications use the finite-family clause of [prop-compactification-refinement]. For three, write $t_i:F_d\xrightarrow{\sim}F_i$ for the comparisons from a single common refinement. Step 8 permits this choice simultaneously for all pairs. Then
$$T_{23}T_{12}=(t_3t_2^{-1})(t_2t_1^{-1})=t_3t_1^{-1}=T_{13}.$$
Also $T_{ii}=\operatorname{id}$ and $T_{21}=T_{12}^{-1}$ by the same cancellation. For the empty family a compactification exists by the nonempty clause, and for a singleton its identity is a common refinement. All equations are natural transformations on the witnessed category of [def-sf-etale-origin-subcategory], the exact domain prescribed by [def-weil-compact-support-candidate]. Thus every asserted finite-family, independence and cocycle clause holds on the stated domain.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $K_0$ be a field, let $X,Y$ be
finite-type $K_0$-schemes, and let
$f:X\to Y$ be a
separated finite-type
$K_0$-morphism. Fix a prime $\ell$, write $\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, and
require that its image in $K_0$ is invertible. Choose a finite extension
$E/\Ql$, an integer $n\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$,
and put $A=A_{E,n}$. The coefficient $A$ is used with the
finite-torsion
constructibility condition. For objects
$c_i=(j_i,\bar f_i)\in\operatorname{Comp}(f)$ in the
compactification category
and a refinement
$u:c_1\to c_2$, the canonical transformation between the
compact-support candidates

$$
R\bar f_{1*,n}j_{1!}
\xrightarrow{\sim}
R\bar f_{2*,n}j_{2!}
$$

is the composite of the proper-composition isomorphism with the isomorphism

$$
Ru_*j_{1!}\xrightarrow{\sim}j_{2!}
$$

on the ambient derived category. These transformations are identities for
identity refinements and are transitive under composition. For any two
compactifications $c_1,c_2$, comparison through a common refinement gives
a natural isomorphism

$$
Rf_{!,n}^{c_1}\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_{!,n}^{c_2}.
$$

Here $R\bar f_{i*,n}$ and $j_{i!}$ are respectively the
derived direct image and
extension-by-zero functors. A common
refinement may be chosen for any finite collection of
compactifications; the resulting comparison is independent of that choice
and satisfies the cocycle condition for triples of compactifications.
The comparison is asserted on the domain declared in
[def-weil-compact-support-candidate]: the complexes of the pro-etale
site that come from the etale site with an
etale-origin witness.

proof.text:
We prove coherence on the full subcategory of complexes
$K=\nu_X^*L$ with $L\in D^+(X_{\Et},A)$, using the comparison
pullback of [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism].
This includes bounded constructible complexes coming from the etale
site. A refinement satisfies $u j_1=j_2$
by [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Use the inverse of
the canonical isomorphism of
[lem-weil-pbc-proper-open-comparison-proetale]:

$$
\alpha_u^{-1}:Ru_*j_{1!}\xrightarrow{\sim}j_{2!}.
$$

The composition isomorphism for derived direct images at finite level,
[lem-weil-derived-direct-image-composition] (1), gives
$R\bar f_{1*,n}\simeq R\bar f_{2*,n}Ru_*$.
Composing with $R\bar f_{2*,n}(\alpha_u^{-1})$ therefore gives the
claimed map of candidates from [def-weil-compact-support-candidate].
It is the identity for an identity refinement, and the composition law
for $\alpha$ makes these maps transitive.

Finally, [prop-compactification-refinement] gives a common
refinement $d$ of any two compactifications. If
$t_i:Rf_{!,n}^{d}\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_{!,n}^{c_i}$ are its maps,
the comparison from $c_1$ to $c_2$ is $t_2t_1^{-1}$.
Given another choice $d'$, choose a refinement mapping to both.
The two resulting maps to each $c_i$ can be made equal by the
parallel-refinement clause; do this for the two $c_i$ successively.
Transitivity then makes the two expressions $t_2t_1^{-1}$ equal.
For three compactifications choose one common refinement, so that
$(t_3t_2^{-1})(t_2t_1^{-1})=t_3t_1^{-1}$.
This proves independence and the cocycle condition on the indicated
full subcategory.

The statement on all of $D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ is no longer part of
the claim: the domain declared in
